detail-recipes.name: White armour
detail-recipes.summary: Clean white armour shaded with soft grey and finished with bright white edges

steps.note: Over a white or pale grey undercoat, leaving room to go brighter at the end.
Thinned half and half, soaking up any pools on flat panels before they dry.
Thin coats back over the flat panels, keeping out of the recesses.
Fine lines along the edges only, as bright white all over looks flat.

detail-recipes.name: White robes
detail-recipes.summary: Creamy white robes over warm grey shadows, with the brightest white kept for the top folds

steps.note: Over the whole robe, as this warm grey becomes the shadow in the deepest folds.
Thin coats over most of the cloth, leaving the grey showing in the folds.
Small steps only, each a little paler, on the raised folds and shoulders.
Only the highest folds and the hem, as going white too early is the usual mistake.

detail-recipes.name: Black robes
detail-recipes.summary: Black cloth that still shows its folds, from an off black with small grey highlights

steps.note: Black with a little blue in thin coats, as black straight from the pot looks flat.
Only the raised folds, keeping more than half of the cloth black.
The sharpest fold tops and hem, or a warm brown grey for dusty, worn robes.
Over everything to calm the greys, then touch the top edges again if needed.

detail-recipes.name: Green cloak
detail-recipes.summary: A mid green cloak with dark folds and soft, warm highlights

steps.note: Over the outside, with a darker green on the lining to frame the figure.
Thinned into the deep folds and under the cloak, not over the flat areas.
On the raised folds, with a touch of yellow if the green looks cold.
Bone mixed into the green reads better on the fold tops than plain white.

detail-recipes.name: Mid blue cloth
detail-recipes.summary: Bright mid blue cloth with dark folds, broad lighter bands and pale edges

steps.note: Thin coats over all the cloth, two or more if it looks patchy.
Thinned and run into the folds and where the cloth meets other parts.
A broad stripe down each fold, blending its sides into wet base blue.
The sharpest fold tops and hem, or short broken strokes for worn cloth.

detail-recipes.name: Brown robes
detail-recipes.summary: Plain brown robes with dark folds, lighter raised folds and a dusty hem

steps.note: Cover all of the robe with a big brush.
All over, so it settles into every fold and seam.
Back over the raised folds, skipping each dark recess, then a finer line on the tops.
Very softly round the hem, building it up slowly for road dust.

detail-recipes.name: Orange cloth
detail-recipes.summary: Warm orange cloth over a red brown base, with cream highlights instead of yellow

steps.note: Over a dark undercoat, as this stays in the folds as the shadow.
Many thin coats from the top of each fold down, leaving the base in the recesses.
Very thin, worked up from the deepest folds and hems.
Thin cream on the fold tops dries as a light orange and looks better than yellow.

detail-recipes.name: Teal cloth
detail-recipes.summary: Deep teal cloth layered up in broad bands to soft aqua highlights

steps.note: Teal can cover weakly, so use thin coats over a grey or blue undercoat.
Cut half and half with medium so it shades the folds without staining the flats.
Broad bands on the raised folds, as small ones leave the cloth looking dark.
Teal with a little bone on the sharpest folds and hem only.

detail-recipes.name: Gold embroidered trim
detail-recipes.summary: A gold thread border painted round a hem, with brown shading and fine stitch dots

steps.note: An even band round the hem, painted on the cloth base coat before any shading.
Over the brown, leaving a hairline of brown each side to frame the band.
Dabbed on, then extra into the sculpted gaps so the raised trim stays bright.
Gold with a little silver, as small crosses or dots along the band for stitches.

detail-recipes.name: Brown fur
detail-recipes.summary: Warm brown fur washed dark, then dry brushed up through khaki to pale tips

steps.note: Thinned a little so it sinks into the fur without filling the texture.
All over, letting it gather deepest at the roots and under the body.
Along the fur with a dry brush, spending longer at the top of the pelt.
Very lightly on the tips, as khaki and bone look warmer than greys.

detail-recipes.name: Grey wolf fur
detail-recipes.summary: Grey wolf fur with a tan underside, a thin black shade and a pale blue grey dry brush

steps.note: Over the back, flanks and tail.
Chest, belly and inner legs, blending into the grey like a real pelt.
Very thin over the whole wolf so it settles between the hairs.
The side of a near dry brush, catching only the tips of the fur.

detail-recipes.name: Black horse coat
detail-recipes.summary: A black horse from a brown grey base, washed black and lifted with soft greys

steps.note: Over the whole horse, with the rider kept off so every part is easy to reach.
All over, soaking up any pools in the mane and tail.
Back over the flat muscles, skipping the gaps between them and next to straps.
Knee ridges and muscle tops, then a fine lighter line inside those.

detail-recipes.name: White horse coat
detail-recipes.summary: A white horse from a soft white with cool grey shadows and a soft pink muzzle

steps.note: Over a white undercoat, as a soft white leaves room for brighter tops.
Cut with plenty of medium and run between the muscles, under the belly and neck.
Back over the tops of the muscles and the mane and tail strands.
Thin on the muzzle and round the eyes, or paint the muzzle black for contrast.

detail-recipes.name: White feathers
detail-recipes.summary: Clean white feathers shaded with a softened grey wash and lifted with white

steps.note: Over all the feathers, or a plain white undercoat does the same job.
A black shade mixed one to one with medium so the flat areas stay pale.
A gentle pass over all the feathers, as the texture catches it well.
The tip of each large feather by hand, thinned a little so it flows.

detail-recipes.name: Brown feathers
detail-recipes.summary: Warm brown feathers built up from a dark base to crisp tan edges

steps.note: Over all the feathered areas.
Over the body feathers, a little heavier on the ones you want brightest.
A fine line on the edge of each large feather by hand for a crisp finish.
Thin over the wing roots and underside to deepen them and tie the steps together.

detail-recipes.name: Bright green gem
detail-recipes.summary: A bright green gem with stacked crescents of light and a white glint

steps.note: Fill the gem, then a thin black shade so it settles where gem meets setting.
A crescent along the lower edge, on the same side on every gem.
A narrower crescent inside the first, with a touch of yellow for extra glow.
A tiny dot in the dark top corner opposite the crescent.

detail-recipes.name: Amber gem
detail-recipes.summary: A warm amber gem from dark orange brown up to golden yellow, shaded with brown not black

steps.note: Fill the gem, as brown shades amber cleanly where black turns it dull.
A curve over the lower half, following the shape of the stone.
A smaller crescent tight to the bottom edge.
One small dot high in the dark corner for the reflection.

detail-recipes.name: Purple gem
detail-recipes.summary: A deep purple gem lit from below with pale lilac crescents and a white glint

steps.note: Fill the whole gem neatly, going darker than feels right.
A crescent round the lower edge.
A smaller crescent tighter to the bottom, with an extra step between on a big gem.
One dot at the top, in the darkest part.

detail-recipes.name: Glass potion bottle
detail-recipes.summary: A glass vial with a level line of bright liquid, a pale surface and a white glint

steps.note: The whole vial in a dark tone of the liquid colour, which reads as glass.
Below a straight line kept level with the base, whatever angle the vial sits at.
Along the top of the liquid and down one side, with a few tiny bubbles.
A diagonal streak on one side of the glass, then gloss varnish on the vial.

detail-recipes.name: Tan leather
detail-recipes.summary: Light tan leather for saddles, belts and gloves, with warm pale highlights

steps.note: Thin coats on the straps, pouches and boots.
All over, then soak up any pools on flat leather.
Back over the raised areas, leaving the creases shaded.
A little flesh tone in the tan, on edges, stitching and a few small scratches.

detail-recipes.name: Red brown leather
detail-recipes.summary: Rich red brown leather from a near black base, lifted to orange brown points

steps.note: Dark red brown mixed with black, over all the leather.
Following the creases on boots, gloves and belts, leaving the deep folds dark.
Just dots and short lines on toe tips, knees, knuckles and edges.
Heavily thinned over everything to warm and richen the leather.

detail-recipes.name: Worn leather
detail-recipes.summary: Battered brown leather with stippled scuffs, scratched edges and a soft glaze

steps.note: A solid coat that stays showing in the folds and scuffs.
Dabbed on raised and lit areas, leaving the base showing between.
Edges, plus tiny criss-cross scratches and nicks on flat panels.
Very thin over the flat areas to soften the contrast, leaving scratches bright.

detail-recipes.name: Sandy stone
detail-recipes.summary: Warm sandy stone for ruins and statues, washed brown and dry brushed up to a pale cream

steps.note: Fewer coats over a sand primer, and a little pink in it gives rose stone.
Thinned with medium so it shades without darkening, soaking up pools at the bottom.
Quick circles with a fully dry brush so it misses the recesses.
A very light flick over the sharpest edges only.

detail-recipes.name: Red brick
detail-recipes.summary: Red brick walls with varied bricks, dark mortar lines and worn pale edges

steps.note: Start a little lighter than you want, as the wash darkens it.
Pick out a few bricks lighter, scattered with no repeating pattern.
All over the wall so it runs into the mortar lines and ties the bricks together.
Catch the brick edges lightly, leaving the mortar lines dark.

detail-recipes.name: Purple skin
detail-recipes.summary: Pale lilac skin washed purple and lifted to soft pale highlights

steps.note: A little strong purple goes a long way, so mix it into pale flesh and a soft white.
All over, with a touch of black added for the deepest shadows.
Back over the muscles and raised features.
Half lilac and half white on the top surfaces, or a pale grey for a softer look.

detail-recipes.name: Scaly snake skin
detail-recipes.summary: Blue green scaly skin with a darker back and a pale belly

steps.note: Thin coats over grey, as this colour can cover weakly.
Cut half and half with medium so it gathers between the scales.
Light flicks on the back and firmer circles on the belly scales.
Mixed with bone on the belly centre, spine tips and face ridges.

detail-recipes.name: Red dragon scales
detail-recipes.summary: Deep red dragon hide dry brushed up from burgundy through red and orange

steps.note: Strong red with a little black and blue, with a second coat on the edges.
Heavy circles all over so every raised scale takes the red.
Into the recesses only, mopping up any pools before it dries.
Orange red then orange on the edges, with a very light touch of yellow last.

detail-recipes.name: Pink tentacles
detail-recipes.summary: Fleshy pink purple tentacles darkening to burgundy, with a wet looking finish

steps.note: Over the tentacles, thinned and blended into any cracks they push through.
All over the tentacles so it gathers in every fold.
Pink towards the tips, blended wet into the burgundy halfway along.
Bumps and ridges, then tiny bone dots and gloss varnish so they look wet.

detail-recipes.name: Bat wing membranes
detail-recipes.summary: Leathery wing skin with dark purple edges and pale flesh glowing in each panel

steps.note: Over the membranes, neatly up to the wing bones.
Softly at first, then heavier in the middle of each panel so it fades to the bones.
A lighter pass over the panel centres, letting the first colour show.
Run neat into the corners where skin meets bone and over the veins.

detail-recipes.name: Iridescent insect wings
detail-recipes.summary: Fly wings from a white top, a purple wash and dabbed rings of green, yellow and pink

steps.note: On the top of each wing and its veins, leaving the lower part darker.
All over, moved about so it marks the veins and cells without pooling.
Green in the middle, then green and yellow, yellow and pink, and pink at the edge.
Thin on the edges and torn tips, then dab a little colour back so it is not chalky.

detail-recipes.name: Chain mail
detail-recipes.summary: Steel mail washed dark in the links, skimmed bright, with optional rust patches

steps.note: Block it in first and roughly, then paint everything else up to it.
Poke it into the links, as air trapped in the rings stops it settling.
A light skim with the side of the brush catches only the raised rings.
Only in a few patches round buckles and lower edges for neglected mail.

detail-recipes.name: Old paper and scrolls
detail-recipes.summary: Warm aged paper for scrolls and labels, with a brown shade, pale edges and fake writing

steps.note: Thin coats, neatly up to the scroll edges.
Over the paper, softening the edge with a damp brush so it ages gently.
The curled edges and the peaks of any creases.
Tiny broken lines or wiggles with the tip to suggest writing, done last.

detail-recipes.name: Natural rope
detail-recipes.summary: Pale sandy rope washed brown and highlighted along each twist

steps.note: Light enough for the wash to darken it.
All over so it runs into the twists.
Short dashes along each twist, following the sculpted strands.
Just the top of each twist, with a fine dark line where rope meets wood.

detail-recipes.name: Natural eyes
detail-recipes.summary: Painted eyes with a dark rim, a soft white eyeball, a dark iris and a tiny glint

steps.note: Fill the eye socket, as this becomes the outline.
Stroke it in from the side, leaving a thin dark rim, as a stark white looks false.
A small dot touching the top lid, so a little white shows below and none above.
One tiny dot or a touch of gloss so the eye looks wet.

detail-recipes.name: Ghostly spirit
detail-recipes.summary: A ghostly body glazed green over white, darkening towards the bottom

steps.note: All the ghostly parts, smooth, as the glazes only glow over white.
Bright green thinned half with medium, over the whole spirit with a big brush.
Each coat starts lower than the last so the colour deepens towards the bottom.
A few thin lines on the topmost points, faces and hands.

detail-recipes.name: Smoke plume
detail-recipes.summary: Dark tinted smoke with the top of each puff lit and the far end palest

steps.note: Thin coats, leaving a gap near any fire or hot part so its glow still shows.
Over most of each puff, as a tinted grey looks better than a plain one.
The raised swirls and the top of each puff, leaving the recesses dark.
Only on puffs farthest from the source, where thin smoke lets more light through.

detail-recipes.name: Light skin with a cool undertone
detail-recipes.summary: Pale skin with pink and purple shadows and a soft rosy flush on the cheeks

steps.note: A pink flesh tone mixed half and half with a light skin tone.
Equal purple and brown, thin, built up slowly in eye sockets and under the jaw.
Very thin on cheeks, ears and lips, as a purple red blush reads truer than red.
Small points on the nose, brow, cheekbones and knuckles.

detail-recipes.name: Light skin with a warm undertone
detail-recipes.summary: Pale golden skin from a tan base, warm brown shadows and creamy highlights

steps.note: Thinned a little, over a light or bone undercoat.
All over, with extra in the eye sockets and under the mouth.
Back over the raised planes of brow, cheeks, nose and chin.
Tiny dots on the nose tip, cheekbones and brows, as a little yellow keeps it warm.

detail-recipes.name: Light skin with an olive undertone
detail-recipes.summary: Light skin muted with a touch of green and shaded with a thin peach tint

steps.note: A light skin tone calmed with a very little dark green.
Thinned, in a pair of light coats rather than one heavy one, so it settles in recesses.
Back over the raised areas, covering a little less with each thin layer.
Knuckles, nose, cheekbones and ears only.

detail-recipes.name: Medium skin with a cool undertone
detail-recipes.summary: A mid brown skin with cool blue and purple shadows and soft pinkish highlights

steps.note: A mid skin tone with a little light blue mixed in, over all the skin.
Thin purple and brown mixed, in the recesses and under the cheekbones.
Very thin under the jaw and nose for cool depth or stubble.
Raised planes of brow, nose and cheeks, then lighter again on the very top.

detail-recipes.name: Deep skin with a cool undertone
detail-recipes.summary: Deep brown skin with blue black shadows, a thin glaze of purple and warm highlights

steps.note: Three thin coats over black, as this is the mid tone.
A skin tone mixed into the base, on brow, nose, cheekbones, chin and lip.
The darkest brown with a dot of dark blue, under cheekbones and in eye sockets.
Very thin in the recesses, then touch the top points back up if needed.
